title: Recent Quality Warnings and the Lapse Allowance of a Wayfare Document Hold: Case Book
content:
This case book applies a rule of the **Driver Services Agreements and Account Standing** product: quality warnings on a Wayfare driver's standing record shorten the lapse allowance days of a document hold, the calendar days that hold may run from its hold start date before it ends in deactivation for document lapse.

## The rule

When the standing record holds two or more quality warnings dated fewer than 6 whole calendar months before the day the allowance is worked out, the lapse allowance days change by -10 days (10 days fewer); when it holds exactly one such warning, they change by -5 days (5 days fewer); when it holds none, they do not change.

Every quality warning counts, whether its basis is the rating or the cancellation rate. A warning dated 6 whole calendar months or more before the day the allowance is worked out does not count.

| Quality warnings dated fewer than 6 whole calendar months back | Change to the lapse allowance days |
|---|---|
| two or more | -10 |
| exactly one | -5 |
| none | 0 |

## Cases (hypothetical, allowance worked out on 2026-10-15)

**Case 1.** A rating warning dated 2026-07-02 and a cancellation-rate warning dated 2026-09-20. Both are fewer than 6 whole calendar months back: two warnings, change -10.

**Case 2.** One cancellation-rate warning dated 2026-05-01 and one rating warning dated 2025-12-10. Only the first is fewer than 6 whole calendar months back: one warning, change -5.

**Case 3.** One rating warning dated 2026-04-15. From 2026-04-15 to 2026-10-15 is 6 whole calendar months, so it does not count: no change.

**Case 4.** One rating warning dated 2026-04-16. Fewer than 6 whole calendar months have passed by 2026-10-15, so it counts: change -5.
